newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HRW wheat harvest set to roll through weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HRW wheat harvest set to roll through weekend.

text.p: Harvesting of the hard red winter wheat crop looked set to roll this weekend in the central U.S. Plains as mostly dry, warm weather was expected to prevail, meteorologists said Friday.
"It looks like this weekend through Monday, most of the thunderstorms should stay north of Kansas," said Jeff Penner, meteorologist at the Weather Center Co.
"There's a slim chance on Sunday morning that one Nebraska cluster turns hard south and enters Kansas, but other than that it should stay dry," Penner said.
"There is pretty favorable weather for the harvest through Sunday," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorlogist.
High temperateratures over the weekend should range from the 80s to low 90s degrees Fahrenheit, Burgio said.

However, more rain was due Monday and Tuesday in Kansas and Oklahoma with amounts of 0.3 to 1.0 inch likely with 60 to 70 percent coverage. Burgio said the rain system also should bring slighlty cooler weather, with temperatures dipping into the low to mid 80s.
"This will probably cause more problems for the harvest," he said.
Burgio said this rain system has the potential to produce hail and high winds similar to those that hit Wednesday in the central U.S. Plains.
Showers may linger Wednesday and Thursday in Kansas, but some areas should dry out then. Temperatures should return to the 80s and 90s Thursday and Friday of next week.
